before: Text typed in a paragraph followed the first of its anchors whose copy showed in another paragraph, skipping nearer anchors whose copies showed in its own paragraph. When a join brought back characters a peer's Enter had moved, and another concurrent split moved characters farther back, the typed text left with the farther anchor while a copy of it also showed, so it showed twice.
after: The nearest anchor with a copy that shows decides. When that copy shows in the text's own paragraph, the text stays there.
reason: Only where a replica shows following text changes; nothing new is written to shared state. Every replica applies the same rule to the same shared state, so replicas converge. Older clients read shared state as before.
